News.title: Rabies deaths are rising. What is going wrong?
News.content:
In a packed intensive care ward in Dhaka, three-year-old Abdul lay paralysed, his tiny body contorted by a rabies infection that had reached his brain.

His mother, Sheuli Akter, 38, sat at his side massaging his legs in the hope that this might loosen his muscles, but it was having no effect. Even his hands and feet were seized up by cramps.

Abdul had been in the hospital for a month but doctors said he was unlikely to live much longer. The infection, they said, had progressed to degenerative encephalitis; the virus had got to his brain.

Abdul was shaking, gripped by fever. His breathing was rapid and panicked, punctuated occasionally by groans of pain.

On his chin was the telltale scar of a dog bite, the source of the infection.

“He was playing outside with the other children,” said Sheuli. “The dog, which was one of those always waiting around outside, suddenly attacked him. They said it went for him because he was the smallest.”

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

News.title: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
News.content:
Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

News.title: Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season
News.content:
Newcastle United 1 Bayer Leverkusen 2

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

News.title: Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn
News.content:
Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Mowbray: It feels like a defeat

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

Sports.title: Loved-up Alex Scott and Jess Glynne strip down to bikinis as couple enjoy romantic Greek getaway
Sports.content:
LIONESSES legend Alex Scott and partner Jess Glynne treated fans to a glimpse of their romantic holiday in a stunning social media post.

The former Arsenal right-back, 41, was part of the BBC’s broadcasting team at the World Cup.



And Scott decided to soak up the sun after seeing Spain win the summer extravaganza.

She has been enjoying a romantic Greek getaway with partner Glynne ahead of the new Premier League season.



The loved-up couple, who started dating in 2023, stripped down to their bikinis in snaps shared on Instagram.

Scott also drove a boat and sipped some wine as she switched off from presenting duties.

And the ex-defender, who has more free time after Football Focus was canned at the end of last season, hit the gym to maintain her physique.

Fans raced into the comments section to rave over Scott and hitmaker Glynne, 36.



One said: “Power couple.”

Another added: “Love seeing your holiday pics. Keep smiling.”



A third chimed in: “You look so happy, lovely couple.”

A fourth noted: “Love this, love you two together.”

And a fifth simply claimed: “Gorgeous.”

Scott bagged a whopping 140 caps for the Lionesses and was part of the squad which came third in the 2015 Women’s World Cup.



She also enjoyed trophy-laden spells with Arsenal, either side of a stint in the USA with Boston Breakers.

But Scott then hung up her boots in 2018 and moved into broadcasting with the BBC.

Sports.title: ‘It comes as a shock’ – Luke Littler’s pal Angryginge releases sweary rant after being ‘dropped’ from Sky Sports
Sports.content:
YOUTUBER Angryginge was left baffled after discovering Baller League will no longer be shown on Sky Sports.

It was reported on Monday that Sky will not air the popular six-a-side league this season after their partnership came to an end.



Baller League will continue to be streamed live on YouTube, Twitch and TikTok, with chief executive Felix Starck pointing out 90 per cent of its audience comes from their own free-to-air channels.

But YouTuber and social media star Angryginge, manager of Baller League team Yanited, had clearly not been made aware of the move and mistakenly thought the league had been dropped by Sky.



After seemingly discovering the news while on a stream, the 24-year-old, who is close friends with darts superstar Luke Littler, said: “I just saw it. Apparently Baller League has been dropped by Sky Sports.

“I don’t know whether that’s part of the plan or whatnot, I haven’t got a f***ing clue.



“But yeah, that’ll be very, very interesting. I’ve got to say, it comes as a shock, it really does.

“That league, reported to be watched more than the Premier League. Why would Sky Sports drop it?

“It makes no f***ing sense to me. Makes zero sense.

“I mean, there’s more to it than that. There’s more to it that meets the eye probably, I don’t know the ins and outs.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The 2025-26 Premier League campaign was Sky Sports‘ most-watched season ever, with viewing figures increased by 25 per cent.

Across all channels, Baller League’s viewership has grown 66 per cent season-on-season with 1.85million tuning in for the Final Four last year.

Baller League was only launched two years ago in Germany, as World Cup-winning stars Mats Hummels and Lukas Podolski backed it heavily.

Those involved with the competition over its first three seasons include KSI, Alan Shearer, Idris Elba, Micah Richards, Gary Lineker, Ian Wright and Chloe Kelly.

Sports.title: Premier League club monitoring their stars’ URINE with state-of-the-art tech after £30m training ground renovation
Sports.content:
IPSWICH are monitoring their players’ URINE in a bid to gain an edge this season.

The Prem new boys have completed a £30million renovation of their Playford Road training base.



Among the swanky new facilities are fancy urinals, kitted out with digital screens that the players must sign into before taking a leak.

This will enable staff members to quickly analyse each star’s hydration levels.



Playford Road had become a source of frustration for former boss Kieran McKenna, with the facilities having previously gone more than 20 years without significant upgrades.

Tractor Boys chairman Mark Ashton believes that the 12 month-renovation has made his side’s training base the best in the area.



Upon Monday’s official opening, Ashton told the East Anglian Daily Times: “There’s nothing like this in east of England. You probably have to go as far as Tottenham to find something on this level.

“Is it helping attract players? For sure. I remember standing with Liam Delap in a muddy field here trying to sell him the vision.

“Now I’m not having to tell prospective signings that there’s something going to come two years down the line, maybe, if we get planning permission.”

McKenna, 40, left Portman Road at the end of last season after guiding his side back to the Prem.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The Northern Irishman was swiftly replaced by former Wolves, Bournemouth and Strasbourg boss Gary O’Neil.

Ashton added: “This helped us get the manager too, by the way. We brought Gary here during the recruitment process because he needed to see if we were real with what we were talking about.

“People interview us as much as we interview them. When you’re trying to persuade people to leave clubs at the top level of world football you’ve got to have a training ground that is first class.”

In addition to fancy toilets, the renovation also includes a hydrotherapy pool, hyperbaric chambers and a cold plunge.



A better gym has been installed, in addition to a modern retina scan entry system and quick boot drying tech.

The expensive project, which Ashton revealed was “under budget” – includes a £1.2million equipment building.

Players will not be able to relax over a game of pool, however, with Ashton reiterating that they’re there to work.

Ashton said: “You’ll notice we haven’t included a pool table, for example.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This is a performance centre that’s been designed to get the maximum out of our players and our staff. We’re giving them the best to underpin a no-excuse culture.”



Ipswich will begin their Prem campaign this Saturday as they host Sunderland.

Sports.title: Unemployed ex-Man Utd ace Memphis Depay, 32, set to re-join club that released him a week earlier
Sports.content:
MEMPHIS DEPAY looks set to re-join Corinthians after agreeing to take a pay cut just a week after being released.

Memphis, 32, registered a total of 20 goals and 15 assists in 79 appearances throughout a two-year stint with the Brazilian giants, where he won the Brazilian Cup and Super Cup in 2025 and 2026 respectively.



However, the winger became a free agent last week when he slammed the club for “unacceptable behaviour” after a previously agreed extension was withdrawn.

However, the Netherlands international put an end to the saga by penning a new contract with the Sao Paulo outfit until 2028.



And Corinthians president Osmar Stabile confirmed the ex-Manchester United ace “significantly” reduced his financial demands.

Stabile said: “Everything’s fine but it was hard work.

“Obviously, you can’t get an international star done very quickly – it was a lengthy process but everything worked out.

“We had a personal meeting and he managed to reduce numbers that his team couldn’t achieve.

“We did what was best for Corinthians, especially in financial terms. [Memphis] Reduced it significantly.

“I don’t want to discuss numbers but he made a considerable reduction because of the circumstances, because of his desire to stay, and because Corinthians needed to find a way to pay.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I believe we can afford this contract.”

According to the BBC, Memphis agreed to waive around £2.9million of the £10.6m owed to him by Corinthians as part of the new two-year deal that is worth a total of £19.1m.

The remainder of the debt, which amounts to £7.6m, will be paid in four instalments, starting in January.

Sports.title: Dream Team Tips: Dominic Calvert-Lewin and other value-for-money strikers capable of plentiful points
Sports.content:
THE new Dream Team season is just around the corner and it’s important managers consider all their options.

Here we have identified five value-for-money strikers capable of healthy returns if everything clicks.

PLAY DREAM TEAM NOW: £100,000 PRIZE POT!



Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£3.5m)

Leeds’ No9 scored 15 goals last season following his free transfer from Everton.



A physically imposing target man, Calvert-Lewin has looked sharp during pre-season and is expected to lead the line for the Whites and remain first-choice penalty-taker.

Daniel Farke’s side have been ultra competitive in the Premier League since the German tactician switched formation and their early fixtures suggest there may be points to be had before the European double Gameweeks become a priority.

Leeds are due to face Nottingham Forest (x2), Brentford, Brighton, Newcastle and Crystal Palace before the first international break.

Igor Jesus (£3m)

Nottingham Forest’s striker bagged 16 goals in all competitions last season.

And while just six of Jesus’ goals came in the league, a double-figure return in the top flight is perfectly achievable this term.

Crystal Palace players earned more than their fair share of points on their way to FA Cup and Conference League triumphs under Oliver Glasner and so Dream Team bosses will be expecting useful returns from Forest’s top performers now the Austrian coach is in charge at the City Ground.

Few would have raised their eyebrows if Jesus started at £3.5m so he should be considered affordable at £3m.



Brian Madjo (£2.5m)

Aston Villa’s teenager won’t be available until September but he’s worthy of a mention nonetheless.

Madjo produced an eye-catching performance against PSG, including a goal, in the Super Cup earlier this month.

He may be just 17 years old but with broad shoulders at 6ft 4in tall he already appears ready for regular Premier League action.



Ollie Watkins (£5m) is the Villains’ main man but rumours about his future still linger and supporters expect Unai Emery to make extensive use of Madjo’s talent this coming season.

Come Christmas, his starting price may seem laughably cheap.

Sports.title: PSG stars arrive to training in luxury cars but fans can’t believe what humble World Cup winner turned up in
Sports.content:
FABIAN RUIZ left fans stunned after turning up to Paris Saint-Germain training in a cut-price car – just weeks on from being crowned a World Cup winner.

The midfielder, 30, got his hands on the sport’s biggest prize when Spain beat Argentina in the final last month.



And Ruiz followed that up by coming off the bench in PSG’s Super Cup win over Aston Villa.

But it appears the former Napoli man has not celebrated his recent successes by splashing the cash on a new motor.



Ruiz was spotted arriving at training, where he waved to adoring fans, in a Smart car.

The humble star’s choice of transport was in stark contrast to some of his big-name team-mates.



Bradley Barcola, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue – along with boss Luis Enrique – were among the members of the squad who drove to PSG’s training base in luxury cars worth more than £100,000.

And fans raced onto social media in disbelief when they realised Ruiz, who was previously a Manchester United transfer target, had not invested in a mega-money motor.

One said: “The car that Fabian Ruiz arrived in looks like a ladybug.”

Another added: “I thought he was a Ballon d’Or contender…”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A third chimed in: “This is stupid.”

A fourth noted: “Reminds me of when everyone thought N’Golo Kante was the most down to earth guy on the planet because he drove a Mini.”

And a fifth claimed: “He’s all about that kilometres per euro.”

But Ruiz could not spearhead PSG to a second piece of silverware in a matter of days as they lost to Lens in the Trophee des Champions.



Both sides finished the contest with ten men and Florian Thauvin notched what proved to be the only goal of the contest.



Last season’s Champions League winners get their domestic campaign underway by hosting Rennes on Sunday.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace make decision on Wilfried Zaha transfer as club legend, 33, returns to training as a free agent
Sports.content:
WILFRIED ZAHA is back training at Crystal Palace but will not be rejoining the club.

The club favourite has been back at the club’s Beckenham training base after completing his contract with Galatasaray in Turkey.



Yet Palace currently have no plans to re-sign the Ivory Coast international who played over 400 games for the club.

The 33-year-old still lives in the area, so he is being allowed to train with Palace while he looks for a new club before the start of the season.



Zaha spent the start of this year playing on loan for former Aston Villa manager Dean Smith at Charlotte FC but the parties could not agree on a permanent deal after his Gala contract ended.

The winger made his senior Palace debut in 2010 after coming through the club’s academy.

He went on to play 458 times for the club, either side of a brief stint at Manchester United and a loan at Cardiff – scoring 90 goals and laying on 54 assists.

Zaha departed Selhurst Park on a free transfer in 2023 despite being offered a lengthy extension.

The 36-cap Ivory Coast international opted to instead move to Turkey, going on to win a league title and domestic cup with Galatasaray.

During this period he went out on two loans; an ill-fated short spell at Lyon and with Smith at Charlotte.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Palace, meanwhile, are still looking to recruit a host of players for new boss Pierre Sage.

Dwight McNeil, £21million winger Anan Khalaili and defenders Takehiro Tomiyasu and Oscar Mingueza have joined but a number of other new arrivals are in the pipeline.

Palace lost their final pre-season friendly 3-0 to Freiburg over the weekend.

They will get their new Prem campaign underway this Saturday with a trip to Everton.

Sports.title: Who is Pep Guardiola’s wife Cristina Serra and when did the former Man City manager split with her?
Sports.content:
PEP Guardiola and Cristina Serra called time on their marriage after more than 30 years together at the end of 2024.

In February 2025, the Sun exclusively revealed the couple had begun divorce proceedings — with both of them even using the same lawyer.

Who is Pep Guardiola’s wife Cristina Serra?

Pep Guardiola was married to Brazilian journalist and writer Cristina Serra.



In January 2025, the couple ended their relationship after living apart for years, with Cristina moving back to Barcelona to run her fashion company.



Determined to avoid an ugly court battle and remain on good terms, they made the bold decision to share the same legal team.

The extraordinarily rare “one couple, one lawyer” divorce means the formal end of their marriage will not be contested by either side.

Spanish journalist Lorena Vazquez, who broke the story of their split, explained: “They want it above all to be friendly for the sake of their children.



“As you can imagine money is not going to be an issue and they have already agreed the initial terms to make sure this separation is the most cordial possible.

“They have a very good relationship, so much so that the same lawyer is arranging the whole thing.

“The divorce is on the way and is being left in the hands of people with their absolute trust.”

She told Spanish TV programme Y Ahora Sonsoles that the couple ended things after Pep signed a two-year extension — keeping him at the Etihad until at least 2027.



Cristina’s family owns fashion store Serra Claret in Barcelona, where she met her future husband when he was just 18 years old.

Pep was doing some modelling for designer Antonio Miro in the shop when he first saw Cristina.

Serra Claret stocks many brands that you see Pep wearing on the touchline including Dsquared2, CP Company and Armani.

Pep previously stated that he trusts his wife so much when it comes to fashion that he lets her pick his clothes for him.

In an interview in January 2024, the footie boss revealed how Cristina even chose his match day outfits.



They want it above all to be friendly for the sake of their children Lorena Vazquez ,

Speaking to Men In Blazers, he said: “My wife is the best in the world at many things, but especially in fashion.

“So she says normally to me, don’t wear this or wear that, so I follow her.

“I am smart enough to know that when people are much, much better than me, follow their advice, and hers is really good.”

When did Pep Guardiola and Cristina Serra get married?

Despite the Manchester City boss meeting his wife as a teenager, they waited a long time to get married.

The pair wed in 2014 in an intimate ceremony in Spain.



They had a private service for close family in the beautiful Spanish area of Catalonia.

Do Pep Guardiola and Cristina Serra have children?

The couple have three children, Maria, Marius and Valentina.

Their eldest daughter Maria is a model who has over 925K followers on Instagram as of February 25, 2025.

She has been very vocal about her love of Man City, a club that dad Pep feels completely at home with.



In 2021, Maria was spotted with ex-Spurs ace Dele Alli in a romantic clinch.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A few months later, they were seen getting lunch together at trendy Mayfair hotspot Novikov, before grabbing a coffee at Starbucks.

However, six months later it was reported that Dele had split with Maria.

Sports.title: US Amateur champion Whaley and Poulter's son named in GB&I Walker Cup team
Sports.content:
US Amateur champion Jack Whaley has been selected in the Great Britain and Ireland team for the 2026 Walker Cup against the USA.

The 22-year-old Englishman forms part of a 10-strong squad, alongside Ian Poulter's son Luke - one of six returning players from the 2025 staging of the event at Cypress Point in California.

Great Britain and Ireland will be looking to beat the USA for the first time since 2015 - and their 16½-9½ triumph at Royal Lytham & St Annes - when the 51st Walker Cup takes place at Lahinch Golf Club in County Clare, Ireland - live on Sky Sports from September 5-6.

Amateur Champion Stuart Grehan and Connor Graham, who will make his third successive appearance, return along with Eliot Baker, Poulter, Niall Sheils Donegan and Tyler Weaver.

The full GB&I team Eliot Baker, England, Tiverton, 23

Ben Bolton, England, Enville, 19

Sam Easterbrook, England, Olton, 21

Connor Graham, Scotland, Blairgowrie, 19

Stuart Grehan, Ireland, County Louth, 33

Josh Hill, England, Fox Den, 22

Luke Poulter, England, Woburn, 22

Niall Sheils Donegan, Scotland, Meadow Club, 21

Tyler Weaver, England, Bury St Edmunds, 21

Jack Whaley, England, Rotherham, 22

(Reserve) Thomas Higgins, Ireland, Roscommon, 23

(Reserve) David Howard, Ireland, Fota Island, 27

Ben Bolton, Sam Easterbrook, Josh Hill and Whaley will make their Walker Cup debuts. Irish pair Thomas Higgins and David Howard have been named as first and second reserve, respectively.

Also returning for another crack at beating the USA is GB&I captain Dean Robertson, who admitted that Whaley would not have been one of his picks to make the team had he not won the US Amateur.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Whaley sensationally chipped in on his way to winning the US Amateur title

The Doncaster-born golfer defeated American Jay Leng Jr in a gruelling 36-hole final on Sunday to become just the third English player in history to win the tournament following on from Harold Hilton in 1911 and current world No 4 Matt Fitzpatrick in 2013.

"Before last week, I wouldn't have seen Jack in the team," Robertson admitted. "But after watching him, the talent he's got and the humility that he's got - the way that he spoke - I'm really excited to welcome him.

"The only downside of that is that if it wasn't for Jack, Tom Higgins would have been in the team, 100 per cent."

What is the Walker Cup? The Walker Cup Match is a biennial 10-man amateur team competition between a team composed of players from Great Britain and Ireland and the USA. It is played over two days with 18 singles matches and eight foursomes matches. The USA leads the overall series 40-9-1.

Robertson added: "We have a really exciting blend of players who have experienced the Walker Cup before and others who have earned their first opportunity through some excellent performances over the last year.

"We have players who have won important championships, performed at the highest level in amateur golf and demonstrated that they can deliver results in international match play.

"We know there will be fantastic support for the team in Ireland and our players will be determined to give those supporters plenty to get behind.

"We learned a great deal from Cypress Point and everyone involved is hugely motivated by the challenge ahead."

Sports.title: England begin new Test cricket era with old captain and no Stokes
Sports.content:
Who's ready for another reset?

England had one of those after their dismal Ashes winter and it started well enough with a Lord's victory over New Zealand, albeit in a two-day rollercoaster ride on a dreadful pitch that meant it was hard to gauge whether any genuine progress had been made.

But that reset soon came crashing down amid familiar old failings of drink-related off-field incidents and witless shots on it. A depleted England side were annihilated at The Oval before a drubbing at Trent Bridge consigned them to a rare home Test series loss.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes took a wicket against New Zealand moments after announcing his retirement from international cricket on day four of the third Test at Trent Bridge in June

Captain Ben Stokes decided he had had enough (bizarrely revealing that midway through a bowling spell at Nottingham and then, the showman that he is, promptly taking a wicket), while coach Brendon McCullum received the tap on the shoulder. Bazball done.

Now we have reset 2.0 with a new skipper - and an old one, too, with Joe Root retaking the job he previously held from 2017-2022 - and a new permanent coach, although not straight away with Stephen Fleming only taking over in earnest ahead of the South Africa trip this winter, leaving Marcus Trescothick in interim charge against Pakistan from Wednesday, live on Sky Sports.

For good or for bad, we knew how England's Bazballers would approach a Test match but with Baz and Ben now gone - the former moving into international retirement, the latter focusing on his role as white-ball head coach - it will be intriguing to see how the style evolves in Root's second term at the helm.

How will England look to play under Root?

Root stressed to Sky Sports' Michael Atherton that he did not want to be seen as a "negative captain" after the issue of England not appearing to even attempt a chase of 273 against New Zealand at Lord's under his leadership in 2021 was brought up - Dom Sibley's dead-batted 60 off 207 balls highlighted that mindset.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root revealed to Sky Sports' Michael Atherton that he has scrapped England's midnight curfew

He spoke glowingly about the effect Bazball had on "taking the fear away" from players and how much he had enjoyed being part of it. He plans to take that into his latest stint as leader but also bring a bit more situational awareness.

In one of Stokes' first interviews as captain four years ago, he was adamant he would never play for a draw. Root, though, explained to Atherton that his England would understand when that was sometimes the way to go. It seems a bit of nuance is coming.

And that is all England fans and followers have been crying out for.

Bazball was not inherently bad, in fact it was inherently good in lifting the team out of the funk they were in after a long period of poor results and oppressive Covid bubbles beforehand.

But it was also inherently flawed and never really sustainable. Root's job now is to channel the best bits of Bazball, add his own stamp and build a winning machine. If England can play as Root bats, then they probably won't go far wrong.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Go back to England's second Test against Pakistan at Emirates Old Trafford in 2016 as Root scored 254

You could never accuse Root of being negative with the blade - we often hear pundits mention how you look up and England's all-time leading run-scorer is on 30 from 30 balls or similar - but he knows when to dial things down and how to win games.

Time for England to start winning again

Winning is not something England are too familiar with in Test cricket at the moment. Their implosion against New Zealand at Trent Bridge in June means they have lost seven and won just two of their last 10 matches. Both of those wins came in two-day toss-ups.

Victories also eluded England during the final part of Root's first spell in charge, with just one across 17 matches before he left in April 2022 but it is worth remembering how taxing that Covid period was and that he didn't always have his best players available.

Root may never be a tactical genius, may not have the gutfeel Stokes had for captaincy - the failed short-ball barrage he deployed against New Zealand while standing in for Stokes at The Oval earlier this summer, dubbed "brainless" by Atherton, was a howler.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain feels Root sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader

Yet he is England's winning-most captain ever, with 27 victories, one more than Michael Vaughan and three more than Stokes and Sir Alastair Cook.

Plus, he feels time has made him realise what he does and does not need to get involved in as skipper and that he must not over-bowl a prized asset in Jofra Archer, something he admitted he was perhaps guilty of in the past.

There is a fear that Root's run-scoring could diminish with the added pressures of captaincy but that did not happen during the Covid era when he had the weight of the world on his shoulders, so it probably won't now either.

Root was not the sexiest choice to be England captain - Sky Sports' Mark Butcher called going back to him "retrograde" and it hardly speaks volumes about succession planning.

However, with Harry Brook's nightclub incident late last year still pretty fresh and Jacob Bethell remaining very nascent in his Test career, and injured now anyway, Root's appointment makes sense.

Image: Stokes (right) will be a big miss for England as they move forward in Test cricket under Root (left)

Stokes retirement leaves big void to fill

He has so many attributes to make this work, including previous experience and the complete respect of his team-mates, but what he doesn't have is Stokes.

Replacing Stokes in the XI is one thing - Dan Lawrence will do it against Pakistan, Sam Curran or Rehan Ahmed could do it in the future. Replacing his aura, all-round aptitude and ability to dig England out of a hole time and time again is almost impossible.

While maybe not the player he was, Stokes' departure means England are worse off.

The feeling, either genuine or just because it would be one hell of a story, is that Stokes could return for The Ashes next summer, a series England will be looking to win for the first time since 2015. Stokes says he won't but it would be no surprise if he did.

For now, though, England need to forget about Stokes and forget about The Ashes. The time has come to win again, starting against Pakistan. Let the new era begin - without the old mistakes.

Sports.title: Sky Sports and The Fast and the Curious announce new partnership
Sports.content:
Sky Sports and The Fast and the Curious have announced a new long-term strategic partnership, ahead of Formula 1's return to action this weekend with the Dutch Grand Prix.

Since launching in 2023, The Fast and the Curious has built a passionate and engaged community by making Formula 1 accessible, entertaining and inclusive. Hosted by Betty Glover, Christian Hewgill and Greg James, the podcast has become known for combining expert insight, exclusive interviews and behind-the-scenes access with humour, warmth and genuine curiosity.

The result is a show that helps new fans feel at home in Formula 1 while offering established followers a fresh perspective on the sport they love.

The overarching goal of the partnership is to help more people discover and enjoy Formula 1 by combining The Fast and the Curious' distinctive editorial voice with Sky Sports' world-class Formula 1 coverage and access.

The partnership will create further opportunities to tell the stories behind the sport, connect fans with the personalities who shape it and bring listeners closer to the action than ever before.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Don't miss the F1 season restart, which kicks off from Friday with the Dutch Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1

Billy McGinty, Sky Sports director of F1, said: "We are always looking to innovate so this partnership offers something genuinely new and exciting for Sky Sports.

"Alongside unlocking commercial benefits, Greg, Betty and Christian have a brilliant ability to relate to the everyday fan, so it presents a great opportunity on both sides to reach new audiences and grow fandom together."

Greg James, 'team principal' of The Fast and the Curious, added: "This is a very large mid-season upgrade! Adding a Sky Sports power unit to our podcast is so exciting.

"When we started The Fast and the Curious, my aim was to create the kind of Formula 1 podcast I've always wanted to listen to; one that was knowledgeable without being intimidating, entertaining without taking itself too seriously, and welcoming to everyone, particularly new fans who wanted to find their gang.

"Partnering with Sky Sports gives us the opportunity to build on everything we've created so far while staying true to what makes the podcast special. We can't wait to see where we can take the show together."

The partnership will bring cross-promotional opportunities with collaborative social posts and the inclusion of The Fast and The Curious content within Sky's digital ecosystem.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See what some of the Formula 1 drivers, including Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, got up to during the summer break!

For OG listeners of The Fast and the Curious podcast, the things they love won't change. Betty, Christian and Greg will continue to bring their unique chemistry, curiosity and passion for Formula 1 to every episode.

One of the podcast's calling cards has been to have F1 drivers on as regular co-hosts. Whether it's finding out that Kimi Antonelli was still at school, learning that Ollie Bearman almost committed 'credit card fraud' (the hosts pretended to have him removed from Silverstone by security as a result) or the more serious discussion with Lewis Hamilton about his desire to make sure LGBTQ+ people feel welcomed by the sport, the gang will continue to unearth new sides of the biggest names on the grid.

The Formula 1 season resumes after the summer break with a Sprint weekend at the Dutch Grand Prix from Friday, with every session live on Sky Sports. Stream Sky Sports with NOW - no contract, cancel anytime

Sports.title: Watch out for Brentford's Sangare - he could be signing of the season
Sports.content:
It's September 2024, and Mamadou Sangare has been called up to the Mali squad for the very first time. As is normal in modern football, new players have to do an initiation song while stood on top of a chair.

As Yves Bissouma introduced him onto the 'stage', the Mali captain asked Sangare what position he'd like to play in the team.

"Yours," Sangare told Bissouma, in a big, bold statement.

"I loved that," Tom Saintfiet, the Mali manager at the time, tells Sky Sports. "He's an open, intelligent person - and confident. He knows what he can do."

Sangare did not end up taking Bissouma's national team spot - they played alongside each other in the Mali team - but the 24-year-old has taken his place as Mali's big talent in the Premier League.

Brentford take on Tottenham Hotspur in the opening day of the season and Sangare will take to the field as the Bees' new record signing. Bissouma - released by Spurs this summer and still without a club - will not.

The Mali midfielder joining Brentford for £39m was deemed quite a coup for the west London club. Sangare was one of RC Lens' most important players as they finished second in Ligue 1 and won the French Cup.

He was subsequently named in Ligue 1's Team of the Year, over Joao Neves and Fabian Ruiz.

Put him in Barcelona's team, and he will have an important role

The 24-year-old could have stayed and played Champions League football with the French side, but instead chose Brentford, when so many other top clubs were circling around him.

"I remember a few months ago when I was talking to him, there were some different names already mentioned," Saintfiet recalls. "There were some top clubs in the English Premier League, the real giants."

Sangare may be new to the average Premier League fan but those who followed Ligue 1 last season will know exactly why this is a promising signing.

The young midfielder effectively earned his status as the 'Elliot Anderson of French football'. He was in a league of his own in terms of ball-winning numbers and defensive statistics.

Image: Mamadou Sangare was one of the top defensive players in Ligue 1 last season

But Sangare is far from simply a defensive midfielder. "No, no," says Saintfiet, who even played Sangare as a wider midfielder in the national team.

"If you talk about ball recovery, tackling, then you look really to the Claude Makelele, the Gennaro Gattuso, the real die-hard No 6. And for me, he's not really a No 6. He's different from that.

"He's more of a No 8 than a No 6, and he can even play as a No 10. His multifunctional qualities are his strengths."

That is good news for Brentford, who have a more than capable No 6 option emerging onto the Premier League scene. If Sangare is the 'Elliot Anderson of French football' then Yehor Yarmoliuk was the 'Elliot Anderson of Brentford' last season, looking at the numbers.

Datawrapper Datawrapper , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable Datawrapper cookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the This content is provided by, which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enablecookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Datawrapper cookies. To view this content you can use the button below to allow Datawrapper cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

So while Yarmoliuk protects the Brentford back four, Sangare can cause opposition players more problems further forward.

"When he has the ball, he is very confident on the ball," says Saintfiet. "He is able to find solutions very fast under pressure, to give good passes, both short and long. So he's much more than only someone who can recover a ball, in my eyes.

"Put him in Barcelona's team, and he will have an important role in such a team - because of his style of playing. He is confident on the ball, he is very smart in his passing. Even if he is strong in ball recovery, he combines that with so many other skills, which is so important in modern football."

The other area where Sangare stands out is his long-range shooting. Only two players in Ligue 1 attempted more shots from outside the box than the Lens players last season - and if Sangare can improve this skill at Brentford, then the hype will only grow.

The early signs are positive - as Sangare opened his Brentford account with a long-range strike in their 7-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt.

Image: Sangare scored this goal from distance in Brentford's 7-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt

"I think he can score a few more goals a season," says Saintfiet. "He has a very good shot, he has a good free kick, but he doesn't use it. In training, I'm always impressed with his shots from distance and during small side games.

"And maybe, sometimes he is too much a team player. He wants to give the chance to another player. He gives a pass when he has the opportunity to take the shot himself. So I think he can be a little bit being more selfish in front of the goal.

"A player who delivers final passes, assists, that's welcome. But if you can have three, four, five goals a season, that will be better. And I think he has that ability to do that. He only has to take now the responsibility to show it."

Sangare may need a bit of time to settle into the Premier League's high-intensity football but he didn't need that time in his debut campaign at Lens last season - becoming an immediate success story after joining from Austrian side Rapid Vienna.

He comes across as a player that the Premier League's 'Big Six' could have easily taken a punt on this summer - and he would have thrived in that environment too.

Brentford

Tottenham Hotspur Saturday 22nd August 5:00pm Kick off 5:30pm

The player who once fought for Bissouma's spot in the Mali team is thinking about bigger and better things.

"For me, Yves Bissouma is a fantastic player," says Saintfiet, comparing the two now. "He has a proven record in the highest level of Europe. Probably Yves could have reached even higher if he had taken different decisions in his career.

"Sangare is starting to be on a real top level now. Brentford is a good step, they have always shown in the past to have an eye for talented players who are maybe less known in England.

"But for me, knowing Mamadou Sangare, Brentford is not his final destination. He can reach the top in England."

Sports.title: Australia make big batting change after shock Bangladesh loss
Sports.content:
Australia have dropped opener Jake Weatherald after their shock home loss to Bangladesh but retained Marnus Labuschagne for the must-win second Test.

Weatherald is the only change in Australia's 13-man squad for the second Test in Mackay, beginning Saturday, where the hosts will look to level the two-Test series after a humbling nine-wicket defeat in Darwin.

Bangladesh's first-ever Test win in Australia put pressure on the national cricket selectors for an overhaul of their aging line-up, with Weatherald replaced by Matt Renshaw in a bid to stabilise the top order.

Weatherald was out for 23 in the first innings and did not score in the second innings of his hometown Test, leaving him averaging 20.36 in his 12 Test innings, with Renshaw a likely contender to replace him to open with Travis Head.

Image: Matt Renshaw is a regular for Australia in ODI and T20 cricket but has not played a Test since 2023

"There was some change to Jake in terms of where he lined up and his movement patterns," coach Andrew McDonald said of Weatherald. "It's always hard to critique small sample sizes on whether it holds up [at international level].

"He dragged one on and drove at one in the first innings and was dismissed; it's probably harder with that smaller sample size to say, 'Yep, that's going to hold up under pressure'. But there was some change though."

Renshaw made his debut in 2016 and played 11 Tests before being dropped in 2018, then was recalled in 2023 for three Tests, but has only played in the shorter formats for Australia since.

He averages 29.31 with one century in 14 Tests although he impressed for Queensland in the Sheffield Shield last season, scoring three centuries among his 499 runs from six matches.

Marnus Labuschagne, who scored one and 31, was retained in the squad despite averaging 25.23 from his last 42 Test innings and not making an international century in nearly three years.

Image: Marnus Labuschagne last made a Test century in July 2023

"It's easy for me to sit here and try to defend that [Labuschagne's form]," McDonald added. "But ultimately, it's 31. It's not a big score. He's lacked runs. He feels that. We feel that. We're working incredibly hard as a coaching group … we've got to get the best out of Marn as well.

"He's had a bit of a lull. He knows that he's gone to work. I think we saw some change in the way that he played, so that's good. Some of that work that he had done feels as though it's stuck up under pressure."

Australia squad: Pat Cummins (captain), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Marnus Labuschagne, Nathan Lyon, Matthew Renshaw, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc, Beau Webster.
